transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... I guess I've just been really bothered by my appearance lately. I work down in production, and I recently started helping out with the safety trainings. But since I started doing that, I just can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look whenever I’m pointing things out to people. 

And then, well, it kind of grew from there. I started thinking my face looks crooked in the company newsletter photos. Other people tell me they don’t see what I'm talking about, but I just can't stop focusing on it.
Is your concern mainly about specific parts of your appearance, like your hands or face, or are you also worried about other areas of your body?

Well, like I was saying, it's really just those two areas. My hands and my face. I haven't really been worrying about the rest of my body. 

It's just... when I'm up there doing the safety trainings, my hands are right out in front of me, and I just can't get over how uneven and wrinkly they look. And then my face looking crooked in those newsletter pictures. So, yeah, it's mainly just those specific parts, even though my coworkers keep telling me they don't see it at all.

latest_inference.note: The patient's concerns are focused on specific parts of their appearance (hands and face) and are accompanied by persistent preoccupation despite reassurance from others. This aligns with the diagnostic criteria for body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). Other candidates related to depressive disorders (F32.x, F33.x) are ruled out due to absence of symptoms suggesting depression.
